set.st: Several versions of one legend. Soldiers from Fort Crawford crossing to McGregor's landing with $8,000 in gold to pay the Fort Atkinson garrison were killed by Indians after burying it on a hill, said to be the Heights; other tellings have a canoe of gold sunk in the Mississippi, a sack buried near Fort Crawford, or $80,000 buried by four of Col. Zachary Taylor's soldiers near North McGregor. Early settlers hunted the hills, and in 1913 a man with a 'gold magnet' came to McGregor to search. In 1937 a girl found an 1851 $10 gold piece on a Mississippi river hill south of McGregor; years earlier three children had found a $20 gold piece on the same side hill a little to the north, and the paper suggested both had washed down from a cache higher in the bluff. A farm west of McGregor was nicknamed the 'Gold Mine' farm for all the digging there. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: Legend with no fixed spot; the pin is the Heights hill named in 1913, and the 1937 coin finds were on the river bluff south of town (about 1-2 km), inside the ring. An 1851 coin is too late for an 1830s-40s payroll, so the finds may be unrelated losses. Effigy Mounds National Monument and Pikes Peak State Park (on the bluffs south of McGregor) are no-dig; McGregor Heights is residential. Access: private / state and federal land near: look only.
